newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River traffic snarled by two accidents.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River traffic snarled by two accidents.

text.p: Marine traffic on the Mississippi River in south Louisiana, already hampered by a capsized barge, was closed to vessels in two other areas Thursday after early morning accidents, the Coast Guard said.
At Laplace, upriver from New Orleans, the river was shut down between mile 120 and mile 132 at midnight when 100 barges broke loose on the river.
Lt. Mike Edmondson of the Louisiana State Police said all 100 barges have been caught. An evacuation order issued after one of the runaway barges began leaking ammonia has been lifted, he said.

At the mouth of the river in Southwest Pass, the Mississippi was closed to traffic in the early morning after the freighter Ariel ran aground, a Coast Guard spokesman said. That is the only river entrance for deep draft vessels.

In Baton Rouge, the river is open during daylight hours to north- and south-bound traffic on a one-way, one vessel at a time basis. After dark, only one-way northbound traffic will be permitted, the Coast Guard said.

Edmondson said divers Thursday will try to drill into a capsized barge containing a volatile mix of benzene and gasoline to measure vapour pressure before lightening the barge on Friday and then righting it with cranes.
The barge capsized Monday evening after a tow with 25 barges hit a bridge at Baton Rouge and broke loose. Two rock barges sank, one is missing, and the others were rounded up.
